objective: Make Naya Power executable and continuously self-tested at the live ChatGPT action boundary.
why: The existing kernel, adapter, and orchestrator were executable but lacked a single live-host entrypoint and the continuous CI gate needed to prove the complete path.
changes: Extended runtime_activation_check.py to require and test the live host bridge
Hardened runtime continuity CI with Python 3.12, compileall, JSON validation, and live-host testing
Changed sparse checkout to non-cone runtime-only patterns so the repository's unrelated legacy long filename cannot block runtime verification
Fixed an actual orchestrator continuation bug where escalation candidates exposed 'reasons' but continuation_for attempted to read 'reason'

observations.failure: Sparse checkout still attempted to materialize an unrelated repository filename that exceeds the runner filesystem limit.

observations.result: Kernel 5/5; Orchestrator 3/3; ChatGPT host adapter 4/4; Live host bridge 3/3; Activation gate ACTIVATED_AND_SELF_TESTED.

learning: A sparse checkout using cone mode can still materialize root-level legacy files; use non-cone path patterns when repository-wide checkout contains unsafe filenames.
Executable integration tests found a real field-name mismatch that unit-level kernel tests did not cover.
A successful constitutional kernel is not enough; the live host seam and continuation path must be runner-tested together.
No external action or production outcome is called verified by the runtime merely because the runtime selected a candidate.
next_action: Run the first real acceptance workload against the actual NayaNET Intelligent Hub source; use source-of-truth inspection, candidate generation, constitutional selection, execution, independent verification, receipt, learning, and immediate continuation.
